observation_summary: The Fraction constructor fails to correctly handle negative values when checking for integer overflow, leading to incorrect fraction results or failure to throw an expected exception.
hypothesis: The overflow checks in the Fraction constructor only verify if the values are greater than Integer.MAX_VALUE, failing to account for negative values that exceed the range of a 32-bit signed integer in the negative direction.
prediction: The code will be updated to use FastMath.abs() on the values being checked against the overflow limit, ensuring both positive and negative overflows are caught.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows that the fix adds FastMath.abs() to the existing overflow checks, which confirms that the root cause was a missing check for negative overflow conditions.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by missing validation logic (a guard) for negative values in the overflow check. The fix adds the necessary absolute value check to the existing conditional statements, which is the definition of a 'Checking' defect.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of FastMath.abs() to the if-conditions checking for overflow.

The bug report comment from Thomas Neidhart explicitly states: 'The overflow check in Fraction does not take negative values into account, it has to be changed to the following: if (FastMath.abs(a0) > overflow) { ... }'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is part of an algorithm, the specific fix is the addition of a missing validation guard (a check), not a rewrite of the computational procedure itself.
